title: Why should you start journalling
paragraphs: For many of us, a work diary is a practical thing. We use them for work to make a note of appointments or meetings, scribbling words next to dates to remind us of something we have to do in the future. But journalling is more about feelings. It’s a personal diary, often kept far from prying eyes, sometimes detailing our secrets and desires. But, when it comes to feelings, what are the benefits to writing things down?

Sometimes it can be difficult to say exactly what we’re feeling. Because of anxiety or frustration, it can be tricky to put your problems into words. For some of us, putting pen to paper and jotting down our thoughts is a much easier process than saying them. But it’s not just about the ease of scrawling words. Writing things down can actually help us to formulate ideas, consolidate emotions, and understand our feelings. There’s something cathartic about making sense of something that is stressing us, annoying us, or getting us down. Writing a narrative of events or a series of words about what is on your mind can help you to focus, and is comparable to a form of meditation. And journalling isn’t just limited to words. Why not include squiggles, doodles or pictures of what’s happening in your life? Maybe the thing that is annoying you most could be best summed up by a caricature. In short, journalling is good for your mental health.

Another thing to consider is that our memories fade over time. What is clear in our minds today may just be forgotten a few years down the line. Logging what’s happening in our lives could trigger memories when we read our diary entries back in years to come, or could act as an insight into our past selves. We can see our development, or be reminded of exciting flashpoints in our lives. The person who was annoying us and you drew a doodle of five years ago may now be a close friend, or something that you were once scared of may now seem funny.
So, if you have something on your mind, it might be good to get things written down. And if something exciting happens, writing about it may help you to remember that wonderful time!

vocabulary.entry: work diary 工作记事本
vocabulary.example: I always keep my work diary updated with upcoming meetings.
vocabulary.translation: 我总是会更新工作记事本，记录下即将到来的会议。

vocabulary.entry: practical /ˈpræktɪkl/ adj. 实用的；切实可行的
vocabulary.example: This tool is very practical for cutting thick branches.
vocabulary.translation: 这个工具用来修剪粗树枝非常实用。

vocabulary.term: make a note of 记录；记下
vocabulary.entry: make a note of 记录；记下
vocabulary.example: I made a note of her phone number before she left.
vocabulary.translation: 她离开前，我记下了她的电话号码。

vocabulary.entry: appointment /əˈpɔɪntmənt/ n. 预约；约定
vocabulary.example: I have a dental appointment tomorrow morning.
vocabulary.translation: 我明天上午有个牙科预约。

vocabulary.entry: scribble /ˈskrɪbl/ v. 潦草地写；随手涂写
vocabulary.example: She scribbled a quick message on a piece of paper.
vocabulary.translation: 她在一张纸上潦草地写了一条短信。

vocabulary.entry: journalling /ˈdʒɜːnəlɪŋ/ n. 写日记；记日志
vocabulary.example: Many people find journalling a helpful way to relieve stress.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人发现写日记是缓解压力的有效方法。

vocabulary.term: prying eyes 窥探的目光；爱打听的人
vocabulary.entry: prying eyes 窥探的目光；爱打听的人
vocabulary.example: She keeps her diary locked away from prying eyes.
vocabulary.translation: 她把日记锁了起来，避免被人窥探。

vocabulary.entry: detail /dɪˈteɪl/ v. 详细记录；详述
vocabulary.example: The report details the progress of the project so far.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告详细记录了项目迄今为止的进展情况。

vocabulary.entry: desire /dɪˈzaɪə(r)/ n. 渴望；欲望
vocabulary.example: She has a strong desire to travel around the world.
vocabulary.translation: 她有强烈的环游世界的渴望。

vocabulary.entry: frustration /frʌˈstreɪʃn/ n. 沮丧；挫败感
vocabulary.example: He slammed the door in frustration after failing the test.
vocabulary.translation: 考试失利后，他沮丧地摔上了门。

vocabulary.entry: tricky /ˈtrɪki/ adj. 棘手的；难办的
vocabulary.example: It can be tricky to tell the two plants apart.
vocabulary.translation: 区分这两种植物可能有些棘手。

vocabulary.term: put pen to paper 动笔写；下笔
vocabulary.entry: put pen to paper 动笔写；下笔
vocabulary.example: She finally put pen to paper and started her novel.
vocabulary.translation: 她终于动笔开始写自己的小说了。

vocabulary.term: jot down 匆匆记下；随手记下
vocabulary.entry: jot down 匆匆记下；随手记下
vocabulary.example: I jotted down his email address before I forgot it.
vocabulary.translation: 我趁没忘记，匆匆记下了他的电子邮箱地址。

vocabulary.entry: scrawl /skrɔːl/ v. 潦草地写；乱涂
vocabulary.example: He scrawled his signature at the bottom of the letter.
vocabulary.translation: 他在信的末尾潦草地签下了自己的名字。

vocabulary.entry: formulate /ˈfɔːmjuleɪt/ v. 构思；规划；确切表达
vocabulary.example: It took her hours to formulate her ideas into a coherent plan.
vocabulary.translation: 她花了好几个小时，才把自己的想法整理成一个条理清晰的计划。

vocabulary.entry: consolidate /kənˈsɒlɪdeɪt/ v. 使巩固；使加强；整理
vocabulary.example: The company is planning to consolidate its business in Europe.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司计划整合其在欧洲的业务。

vocabulary.entry: cathartic /kəˈθɑːtɪk/ adj. 宣泄情绪的；使人舒畅的
vocabulary.example: For her, singing is a cathartic activity that relieves stress.
vocabulary.translation: 对她而言，唱歌是一种能缓解压力的宣泄方式。

vocabulary.term: make sense of 理解；弄懂
vocabulary.entry: make sense of 理解；弄懂
vocabulary.example: I can’t make sense of this instruction manual.
vocabulary.translation: 我看不懂这本说明书。

vocabulary.term: get sb down 使某人沮丧；使某人消沉
vocabulary.entry: get sb down 使某人沮丧；使某人消沉
vocabulary.example: The constant rain was really getting me down.
vocabulary.translation: 连绵不断的阴雨天气真的让我很消沉。

vocabulary.entry: narrative /ˈnærətɪv/ n. 叙述；讲述；故事
vocabulary.example: The novel has a gripping narrative that keeps readers hooked.
vocabulary.translation: 这本小说的叙事扣人心弦，让读者欲罢不能。

vocabulary.entry: comparable /ˈkɒmpərəbl/ adj. 类似的；可比较的
vocabulary.example: The situation is comparable to the one we faced last year.
vocabulary.translation: 目前的情况和我们去年遇到的很相似。

vocabulary.entry: meditation /ˌmedɪˈteɪʃn/ n. 冥想；沉思
vocabulary.example: She practices meditation for ten minutes every morning.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天早上都会冥想十分钟。

vocabulary.entry: squiggle /ˈskwɪɡl/ n. 潦草的线条；弯弯曲曲的笔迹
vocabulary.example: The child drew squiggles all over the piece of paper.
vocabulary.translation: 这个孩子在纸上画满了歪歪扭扭的线条。

vocabulary.entry: doodle /ˈduːdl/ n. 涂鸦；随手画的图画
vocabulary.example: He often draws doodles during long meetings.
vocabulary.translation: 他在冗长的会议中经常随手涂鸦。

vocabulary.entry: sum up 概括；总结
vocabulary.example: The teacher summed up the main points of the lesson in five minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 老师用五分钟总结了本节课的重点内容。

vocabulary.entry: caricature /ˈkærɪkətʃʊə(r)/ n. 夸张的描绘；漫画；讽刺画
vocabulary.example: The magazine published a caricature of the famous politician.
vocabulary.translation: 这本杂志刊登了一幅那位知名政客的讽刺漫画。

vocabulary.entry: mental health 心理健康
vocabulary.example: Schools should pay more attention to students’ mental health.
vocabulary.translation: 学校应该更关注学生的心理健康。

vocabulary.entry: fade /feɪd/ v. 逐渐变淡；逐渐模糊；褪色
vocabulary.example: The memory of that day has faded over the years.
vocabulary.translation: 这些年来，那天的记忆已经渐渐模糊了。

vocabulary.entry: log /lɒɡ/ v. 记录；记载
vocabulary.example: The software logs all the users’ activities on the computer.
vocabulary.translation: 这款软件会记录用户在电脑上的所有操作。

vocabulary.entry: trigger /ˈtrɪɡə(r)/ v. 触发；引起
vocabulary.example: The smell of freshly baked bread triggered memories of her childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 新鲜出炉的面包香味勾起了她对童年的回忆。

vocabulary.entry: insight /ˈɪnsaɪt/ n. 洞悉；深刻理解；洞察力
vocabulary.example: The book gave me a new insight into human behavior.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书让我对人类行为有了新的深刻理解。

vocabulary.entry: flashpoint /ˈflæʃpɔɪnt/ n. （事件的）爆发点；关键时刻
vocabulary.example: The protest became the flashpoint for a series of political changes.
vocabulary.translation: 这场抗议成了一系列政治变革的导火索。

sentences.english: For many of us, a work diary is a practical thing.
sentences.chinese: 对我们很多人来说，工作日志很实用。

sentences.english: We use them for work to make a note of appointments or meetings, scribbling words next to dates to remind us of something we have to do in the future.
sentences.chinese: 我们用它来记录工作上的预约或会议，在日期旁随手写下文字，提醒自己将要处理的事情。

sentences.english: But journalling is more about feelings.
sentences.chinese: 但日记（情感记录）则更侧重于内心感受。

sentences.english: It’s a personal diary, often kept far from prying eyes, sometimes detailing our secrets and desires.
sentences.chinese: 它是一本私人日记，往往会被藏起来，远离他人窥探的目光，里面有时会详细记录我们的秘密与渴望。

sentences.english: But, when it comes to feelings, what are the benefits to writing things down?
sentences.chinese: 但当涉及到情感表达时，把想法写下来究竟有哪些好处呢？

sentences.english: Sometimes it can be difficult to say exactly what we’re feeling.
sentences.chinese: 有时候，我们很难准确说出自己的感受。

sentences.english: Because of anxiety or frustration, it can be tricky to put your problems into words.
sentences.chinese: 因为焦虑或沮丧的情绪，想要把内心的烦恼用语言表达出来并非易事。

sentences.english: For some of us, putting pen to paper and jotting down our thoughts is a much easier process than saying them.
sentences.chinese: 对有些人来说，拿起笔把想法写下来，比口头表述要容易得多。

sentences.english: But it’s not just about the ease of scrawling words. Writing things down can actually help us to formulate ideas, consolidate emotions, and understand our feelings.
sentences.chinese: 但这不仅仅是因为随手书写的便捷性，把事情写下来其实能帮助我们梳理思路、稳定情绪，进而理解自己的内心感受。

sentences.english: There’s something cathartic about making sense of something that is stressing us, annoying us, or getting us down.
sentences.chinese: 当我们弄清楚那些让自己倍感压力、心烦意乱或情绪低落的事情，会有一种宣泄情绪的治愈感。

sentences.english: Writing a narrative of events or a series of words about what is on your mind can help you to focus, and is comparable to a form of meditation.
sentences.chinese: 将发生的事情写成一段文字，或是把心里的想法记录下来，能帮助我们集中注意力，这堪比一种冥想方式。

sentences.english: And journalling isn’t just limited to words. Why not include squiggles, doodles or pictures of what’s happening in your life?
sentences.chinese: 而且写日记并不局限于文字，你完全可以在日记里画些线条、涂鸦或是生活场景的简笔画。

sentences.english: Maybe the thing that is annoying you most could be best summed up by a caricature.
sentences.chinese: 也许那个最让你心烦的人或事，用一幅夸张的漫画就能精准概括。

sentences.english: In short, journalling is good for your mental health.
sentences.chinese: 简而言之，写日记有益于心理健康。

sentences.english: Another thing to consider is that our memories fade over time.
sentences.chinese: 还有一点需要考虑的是，人的记忆会随着时间流逝而模糊。

sentences.english: What is clear in our minds today may just be forgotten a few years down the line.
sentences.chinese: 今天在脑海里清晰无比的事情，几年后可能就会被彻底遗忘。

sentences.english: Logging what’s happening in our lives could trigger memories when we read our diary entries back in years to come, or could act as an insight into our past selves.
sentences.chinese: 记录下生活中发生的点滴，未来某天翻看日记时，既能唤醒尘封的记忆，也能让我们窥见过去的自己。

sentences.english: We can see our development, or be reminded of exciting flashpoints in our lives.
sentences.chinese: 我们能从中看到自己的成长，或者回忆起人生中那些激动人心的高光时刻。

sentences.english: The person who was annoying us and you drew a doodle of five years ago may now be a close friend, or something that you were once scared of may now seem funny.
sentences.chinese: 五年前那个让你厌烦到忍不住画成涂鸦的人，如今或许已成了挚友；而曾经让你恐惧不已的事情，现在回想起来可能会觉得好笑。

sentences.english: So, if you have something on your mind, it might be good to get things written down.
sentences.chinese: 所以，如果你心里有事，不妨把它写下来。

sentences.english: And if something exciting happens, writing about it may help you to remember that wonderful time!
sentences.chinese: 而如果有令人开心的事情发生，把它记录下来也能帮你留住那段美好的时光。
